correctness.rationale: PASS: Circulant diagonalization gives real eigenvalues L_{n,j}(t) as finite Gaussian Fourier sums. Poisson summation yields a positive full-lattice theta series bounded below by sqrt(π/t)exp(-π²/(4t)); the finite-cycle truncation error has uniform bound 2exp(-tn²/4)/(1-exp(-tn)). For all t∈[a/n,1], a>π, the error/theta ratio tends to zero uniformly in index and t at exponential rate exp(-(a²-π²)n/(4a)); for t>=1 strict diagonal dominance holds. For c<π, the proof explicitly chooses a near-Nyquist Fourier index for each of four congruence classes. The even-n omitted-tail identity has positive limit (1-e^-c)/(1+e^-c); the odd-n sine-weighted identity has positive limit (1-e^-c)/(2(1+e^-c)^2) after 1/n normalization. Since the missing tail is exp(-cn/4) up to polynomial factors but full theta is O_c(sqrt(n)exp(-π²n/(4c))), the finite eigenvalue is negative eventually. These exact inequalities prove the all-n squeeze and finiteness of τ_n. Independent 100-digit Fourier calculations confirmed selected above-threshold positivity and eventually negative below-threshold witnesses, with n=63 below-threshold witness still positive (permitted by the asymptotic quantifier). The n=83 and 103 near-Nyquist witnesses were negative. No claim of finite-n unique crossing is made.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge PASS: Feragen–Lauze–Hauberg establish geometric obstructions to positive definiteness at all bandwidths, while Da Costa–Mostajeran–Ortega prove that no fixed Gaussian scale works on the full continuous circle, using finite equispaced samples. Those theorems do not state a simultaneous high-parameter positive interval or its π/n deterministic threshold. The 2016 finite-sample open-problem paper does not determine the coefficient. The highly plausible Wood 1995 circle covariance paper remained abstract-only; potential hidden coverage is a named risk, not sufficient alone to fail originality. The full leading constant and all-congruence witness appear not covered in inspected evidence.

value.rationale: PASS: Squared-geodesic Gaussian Gram matrices on finite uniform cycles are canonical covariance matrices with a real positive-definiteness obstruction. The leading last-failure scale across every cyclic order, with a simultaneous all-larger-t guarantee, is quantitatively useful for choosing sampling-dependent bandwidth. The π coefficient emerges from a nontrivial competition of Poisson theta tails and finite truncation, with a sharp even/odd Fourier witness. It is not merely the standard fixed-bandwidth infinite-circle non-positive-definiteness theorem.

final_claim: For every n>=3 define K_n(t)_{ab}=exp(-t d_n(a,b)^2), with cyclic shortest-path distance, and τ_n the supremum of t giving a negative eigenvalue. Then nτ_n→π. For every eps∈(0,π), for all sufficiently large n the matrix is strictly positive definite simultaneously for every t>=(π+eps)/n, while K_n((π-eps)/n) has a negative eigenvalue. No finite-n monotonicity assertion.
